crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: GDP Nowcasting
children.blurb: GDP nowcasting is the practice of estimating the current quarter's gross domestic product before the official statistic is published.

children.name: Reading Central Bank Communication
children.blurb: Reading central bank communication is the systematic study of what monetary policy makers say and write, from rate decisions and statements to minutes, speeches, interviews and press conferences.

children.name: Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis
children.blurb: Synthetic populations for policy analysis are artificial datasets of people, households, firms, or places that match the statistical properties of a real population.

children.name: Climate and the Economy
children.blurb: Climate and the Economy in macroeconomic econometrics covers how weather shocks, gradual warming, and climate policy affect aggregate outcomes such as output, inflation, employment, investment, and trade.

children.name: Agent-Based and Game Theory Models
children.blurb: Agent-based and game theory models in macroeconomic econometrics simulate economies as populations of heterogeneous agents who interact according to strategic rules, rather than as a single representative household or firm.

sections.body: Macroeconomic econometrics is the practice of measuring and forecasting whole economies with statistical models. AI is used to handle high-frequency data, text, and large simulation, not just to fit small linear equations. GDP Nowcasting uses machine learning to estimate current output before official figures arrive. Reading Central Bank Communication applies language models to policy statements and speeches to gauge tone and likely rate path. Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis builds simulated households and firms to test tax or transfer changes. Climate and the Economy links weather, energy, and damage data to macroeconomic outcomes, while Agent-Based and Game Theory Models simulates many decision makers interacting, including strategic behaviour.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are well established, like short-horizon nowcasting with mixed-frequency data and text sentiment scoring of central bank language. Other tasks remain fragile. Nowcasts can fail at turning points, and text models can mistake boilerplate for signal. Synthetic populations are only as good as the survey and administrative data used to calibrate them, and they struggle with rare shocks. Climate-economy models carry deep uncertainty about damages, adaptation, and tipping points. Agent-based models can reproduce patterns but are hard to validate and estimate, and honest limits include data revisions, regime change, and the gap between correlation and causal policy advice.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages fit as a chain from measurement to interpretation to simulation. GDP Nowcasting is the entry point for tracking current activity in real time. Reading Central Bank Communication shows how AI extracts policy signals from language, which feeds expectations into the nowcast. Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis moves from measurement to counterfactual distributional questions. Climate and the Economy adds a physical and long-horizon stress to the same macro framework. Agent-Based and Game Theory Models provides the microfoundations for strategic interaction and emergent outcomes, and a reader would go to each page for a different layer, from data to text to simulated agents.
